items.desc: Tangerine arrives on Butter Sessions with Language of Sound, the second offering from the Melbourne / Naarm-based artist Clementine Girard-Foley. Four forward-thinking tracks that nod to techno, electro, IDM and bass music, with a playful, slightly rude and quietly optimistic mood that Tangerine pulls off with ease. credits Written and produced by Clementine Girard-Foley. Mixed by Borgqueen at Syntonix. Mastered by Corey Kikos. Artwork and design by Maryos Syawish.
items.title: Tangerine - Language of Sound

items.desc: Welcoming Kamome to the BSRMIX! The Tokyo-raised DJ and Vinyl Youth member spent some time in Melbourne / Naarm, where he quickly found his place in the local music scene. His eclectic selections made their way into DJ booths and onto dancefloors across town, leaving a lasting impression since his return to Japan. We're very happy to share this recording from his set at Tomoya's secret space at Strawberry Fields 2025. P.S. There are a few moments of silence in the recording, a little reminder of the unpredictable nature of these bush parties (the sound system shut down!)
items.title: BSRMIX #174 - Kamome

items.desc: Celebrating his recent release with Sleep D on Butter Sessions, the elusive Mosam Howieson returns for his third BSRMIX, a 4 hour serving of pure techno power. Sink in and gear up for his live set at the Syphon Filter launch party this Saturday, October 17. (DM us for ticket access)
items.title: BSRMIX #173 - Mosam Howieson

items.desc: Sleep D and Mosam Howieson join forces for an EP that traverses peak-time pressure and deep hypnotic terrain. Opening with ‘Syphon Filter’, a monstrous techno steam train that sparked the collaboration for the record, starting over five years ago. Industrial klanging to a banging beat. Simple and effective. Chugging along, ‘Inertia’ and ‘Mirror Pool’ offer respite with a psychedelic and emotive strain of techno. Rounding out the release, Dutch producer Konduku reshapes one Mirror Pool into a stripped-back, fluid remix. Refracting the source material through his distinctive palette.
items.title: Sleep D & Mosam Howieson - Syphon Filter (Inc Konduku Remix)

items.desc: 1. This Dog Goes Subwoof 2. Sleaze 3. Rhinestones 4. Hummingbird Mabel debuts on Butter Sessions with Rhinestones, a collection of pounding progressive house excursions that lean into the deep end. Balancing blissful nostalgia with a sharp modern touch, the EP draws on classic prog and hard house sounds without getting stuck in the past. Driving rhythms, naughty amounts of low end and all the right bleeps and SFX to send your serotonin soaring. Shine on, you crazy Rhinestone.
items.title: Mabel - Rhinestones (BSRCD01)

items.desc: Welcoming back 2 of our earliest BSRMIX contributors, Luke Bruin (Mix 001) and Louis McCoy (Mix 008). Recorded live from Strawberry Fields 2025, holding down the deep sound they’re experts at whilst picking up the pace since ether inaugural BSRMIX’s from 12+ years ago. These two were an inspiration to us in the early BSR days and we’re honoured to have these selectors on mix 172.
items.title: BSRMIX #172 - Louis McCoy & Luke Bruin (Recorded live at Strawberry Fields Festival 2025)

items.desc: Sleep D in the mix, recorded live at RITMO festival, Granada, Spain! Two hours of mountain top power sandwiched between Lukas Wigflex and Aurora Halal. Featuring a couple of upcoming Butter Sessions tracks by Tangerine, Sleep D & Mosam Howieson and more. Enjoy!

items.desc: On The Arboretum, Analogue Attic co-founder Alex Albrecht leans further into the dancefloor, channelling the more hypnotic and driving energy that Butter Sessions is known for. Across the five tracks, listeners are treated to Albrecht's signature melody-driven deep house, bolstered by intricate rhythms, a deeper low end, and hypnotic loops designed for larger systems and later hours. The tracks are playful yet serious, functional yet full of personality. There’s the joy of long blends and the tiny details that bubble up in the mix: field recordings from time spent away, nostalgic archival mat…
items.title: Alex Albrecht - The Arboretum (BSR047)

items.desc: On Butter Sessions, Iti presents Colourful Choices, a collision of vivid synth melodies and fractured drum rhythms. The title nods to the multicoloured lights and patch cables of his synths - the primary source of the record's motifs. The EP opens with the title track Colourful Choices, beginning with a shimmering string-synth that bends and twists into a playful, colourful melody. It's joined by a punchy drum-machine rhythm before descending into a gritty, driving bassline. Exit shifts the energy with garage-electro edge, its weighty low-end anchoring robotic synth stabs before erupting into…
items.title: Iti - Colourful Choices EP (BSD09)

items.desc: Welcoming Flud to the BSRMIX! Better known as Ewan Jansen, Flud is the latest incarnation of the Red Ember Records boss. Self-described as an "amphibious, rhythmical live experience fusing analog and digital relics under a comfy skyline," BSRMIX 162 delivers exactly that. Over an hour of ambient and downtempo-leaning live electronics, recorded live at Skydiver Records in Naarm/Melbourne in early 2025.
items.title: BSRMIX #162 - Flud

items.desc: Very excited to have Iti join the BSRMIX series before his soon to be announced EP on Butter Sessions Records. Itrat Memon is an Irish/Australian producer, DJ and co founder of Pocketmoth record label, based in London via Brisbane/Meanjin. Expect crispy beats and deep synthesis on this 1Hr26min mix. @iti_mqn

items.desc: Eora’s dub-techno tastemaker Command D and Naarm’s harmoniser of the emotive and abstract Zara combine for Gravity Reset, a collaborative four-tracker on Butter Sessions. Both producers are equally nestled with love into Australia’s underground, with releases on beloved labels like Animalia and Pure Space. Command D also boasts refined live sets heaving in sub-bass, while Zara's celebrated for boundary-blurring productions and her Kinesis imprint championing the local scene. On Gravity Reset, they meet in lockstep, delivering trance-inducing offerings rooted in a shared love of rhythm, space …
